chapter: Passion, family and the musician's life
title: Music as passion, not a job
summary: Finding a sound takes years; he says music must be a passion and he would die if he could not play, though the life demands sacrifice.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: So in some sense it’s almost comical to tell a 19-year-old kid you’ve got to find your own sound man. I mean they’re not grown up yet. I guess they can start on it.

Yeah, but no one’s going to find their own sound when they’re 19 or 20. It’s very unusual. Because like you said, they’re incredibly young. But I think that they have to be encouraged to start that process at a young age, if they’re going to really go on and consider playing this music for their life, for their work, for their passion. Because it has to be a passion. It’s not a job.
Go on about that, it’s not a job.

You can’t — I don’t consider what I do as having a job. You know being a musician is inherently wrapped up in who I am as a human being and I can’t separate those two things, between being a musician and being alive on this planet as a human being. And I mean there’s a lot of passion there, and I feel like a lot of times I feel like if I couldn’t play that I would die. I just feel it’s just so much a part of my existence in the world, and I try to instill that in young musicians, like this has to be something that you absolutely have to do, and it’s almost like if you have a choice you should do something else in a way. Because it’s not an easy life, being a musician. There’s a lot of sacrifices involved. I mean just the amount of time that you have to practice, that’s just a small one. I mean if you start making it and becoming successful then you’re away from home. If you have a family you don’t see your kids grow up. You know it’s not necessarily always an easy existence.
